## The game in one page

Every builder reads this page before an item, and the reviewer reads it with the diff (decided 28 October 2026). Most questions an item raises answer themselves from it; an item's own rule never quietly overrides it. Haakon: "Everything has to happen through giving a message and following up on promises." And: "Freedom to do, consequences that emerge."

- **Nothing happens unless someone orders it.** The engine moves people, coin and goods, resolves fights, rolls skills and keeps the facts; it never acts for anyone. A king may automate his own acts with standing and scheduled orders, but the engine never does it for him.
- **Words are words.** Offers, promises, threats and deals travel as messages carried by characters, and bind nobody. The engine records a deal only when it is sealed on a tablet, and then only that it was sealed and, later, whether it was kept.
- **Keeping a promise is an act.** Paying a fee, sending tribute, returning a runaway or granting passage happens only when the one who promised orders it. He never has to. If a sealed tablet said he would and he does not, the engine records the broken deal, and others learn of it as news.
- **Everything is somewhere, and everything travels.** People, coin, grain, tablets and news move at the pace of the roads and can be waylaid; nothing is known or delivered at a distance without someone carrying it.
- **Skills set the odds; characters decide.** Nobody sees another's skills or the truth except through evidence they gather.

Worked examples, each with the wrong turn to avoid:

- **Hiring.** A king, or any character he sends, carries an offer to the man wherever he is; the man answers; a sealed tablet records the job, its fee and its terms. A job is always an errand: what to do, where and by when, a part paid now and a part on completion; a long stay, such as a resident envoy's or a posted spy's, is an errand with a deadline. Not: hiring only at the court where the man stands, a job that exists without anyone carrying the offer, or a post whose errands come free.
- **Paying the fee.** The employer orders each payment, by hand or by his own standing order ("pay on delivery"). Unpaid is unpaid. When the errand ends, it ends: renewing it is a new offer, which the employer may automate and the man must still accept. Not: the engine paying the rest automatically, assuming half now when nobody said so, or renewing a deal nobody made.
- **Prices.** Every fee is what the two sides agree, and goods sell by supply and demand in the markets. What others were paid is only what a character has heard, and he bargains from it. Not: a going rate or a floor set by the engine.
- **Privileges.** Governorship and command of an army are grants of authority, not jobs: what the man gets is what holding them gives him, the yield or the spoils passing through his hands, the men and his standing. The king takes the grant back by sending word, and enforces that only with troops. Not: a governor or commander on a fee, or a grant revoked at a distance at once.
- **Captives.** A captive's purse stays on him, where he is held; his captor may order it taken. Not: the purse passing to the captor by itself.
- **Memory.** A model character chooses what to keep when his older notes are condensed, so an old betrayal that matters to him survives; a script character weighs old news less as it ages, by his own formula, and never loses it; the tablets and a court's records stay as they are. Not: a rule that forgets after so many seasons.
- **Reports.** A report is the servant's own words: he may leave things out or lie, and the engine checks only that he delivered it. If he then sells what belonged in it, to his employer or to anyone the employer hears of, that is evidence of a broken job, which the employer may act on and tell others. Not: the engine judging whether a report was complete or true.
- **Debts.** A debt tablet records the debt; repaying is the borrower's order, collecting is the creditor's errand, and a king who holds the tablet may collect or sell it. Not: automatic repayment or automatic default.
- **Reputation.** A court learns that a king broke a tablet, dismissed a servant early or paid badly when someone tells it or shows the tablet. Not: a record known to all at once.
- **Passage.** Granted by tablet or by order; the grantee learns of it when the grantor's word reaches him, or when his troops pass unchallenged. Not: told at once.
- **Hard acts.** Seizing a man's hoard, dismissing a servant, levying every man of a province: all allowed, at their real cost, and recorded as facts others may hear of. No rule punishes them: what follows comes only from what the act does to the people's contentment and to characters' incentives. Not: forbidden, or punished by a rule of its own.
